title: AI Infrastructure Power and Cooling
summary: Connect high-density compute to power, heat, cooling, and community infrastructure considerations.
objectives: Explain the compute-density to power-density to heat relationship.
Identify safe operational responses to synthetic power and thermal concerns.

vocab.def: Power demand concentrated within a physical area or equipment footprint.
Heat that a system must manage in a scenario.
The modeled amount a system or facility resource can support.

sections.heading: Compute has physical effects
sections.body: High-performance compute can increase power demand in a smaller space, which increases heat-management and cooling requirements. Facilities differ, and not every AI system uses liquid cooling.

sections.heading: Connect the domains
sections.body: Consider power, temperature, airflow or liquid-cooling context, capacity, monitoring, and reliability together. Electricity and mechanical service remain qualified-professional work.

practice.prompt: A high-density workload raises power draw and rack temperature in a synthetic scenario. What is safe?
practice.answer: Record the telemetry, compare stated capacity, and escalate through an authorized operations process.

quiz.question: What relationship is useful in AI infrastructure reasoning?
options: Compute density can affect power density, heat, and cooling demand
AI workloads have no physical impact
quiz.answer: Compute density can affect power density, heat, and cooling demand

lab.objective: Interpret synthetic AI power and cooling telemetry.
